To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transfer of a loop-to-loop electromagnetic signal across a thin metal screen with Drude-type dispersive behavior can be described by a simple analytical formula that is valid for arbitrary signal bandwidth and that the signal transfer is not affected by the dispersive properties of the screen if the signal bandwidth is small compared with the plasma frequency.

the transmission of a loop-to-loop pulse across a thin metal screen is significantly affected by the Drude-type dispersion of the screen, and that a simple model based on the effective dielectric permittivity of the metal can be used to describe the transmission behavior in a wide frequency range, including the optical regime.

the loop-to-loop signal transmission coefficient of a thin Drude metal screen is a function of the frequency, thickness and resistivity of the screen, the loop separation, and the loop radius, and that it can be expressed in a compact analytic form that is valid for arbitrary screen thicknesses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the analysis of electromagnetic wave transmission across a thin metal screen, which separates two identical transmission lines, and the analysis of the electromagnetic field in the vicinity of the screen, in particular the field distribution on the screen itself.

the analysis of the time-domain response of a metal screen of finite thickness to an electromagnetic field that is incident from one side, and that is characterized by a Drude-type frequency dispersion.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the plasmonic effects of the metal screen can be taken into account by using a Drude-type model, but the Drude-type model has to be modified in such a way as to include the effects of the finite thickness of the metal screen.

the plasmonic properties of the metal screen can significantly alter the transfer of electromagnetic signals through the screen and the resulting interference, but the plasmic effects do not alter the essential features of the transfer and interference, which are determined by the geometry of the problem.
the loop-to-loop pulsed signal transfer through a thin metal screen is a complex function of the screen thickness, the frequency of the signal, and the distance between the loops.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the plasmonic properties of the thin screen are responsible for a very strong enhancement of the electromagnetic coupling between the two loops, with the coupling being strongly dependent on the frequency of the electromagnetic signal and the thickness of the screen.

the loop-to-loop transfer of pulsed electromagnetic signals across a thin metal screen with Drude-type dispersive behavior can be described analytically in the time domain by a simple convolution operation.

we have found that, in the presence of a thin metal screen with Drude-type dispersive behavior, the electromagnetic signal transfer between the two sides of the screen is significantly different from the case of an ideal, perfect electrical conductor screen, even when the thickness of the metal is very small compared to the wavelength of the electromagnetic signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the time-domain analysis of this canonical problem, which is of fundamental importance to integrated-circuit design, can be carried out in closed form for the case of a Drude-type dispersion relation for the metal.
the plasmonic response of a thin metal screen is not negligible even at optical frequencies.

the plasmonic response of the metal is not just a perturbative effect, but it can have a dramatic influence on the electromagnetic signal transfer across the screen, especially when the signal is pulsed, as in a digital system.
